subject: HyperCloud pricing: request for custom per-token band + 12mo commit
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@hypercloud.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing bands and commit question

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — the engineering team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile. We're preparing an internal budget and procurement packet and wanted to check: for a 12 month firm commitment (estimated 9B tokens / month), can we get an incremental per-token band below the published rate-card?

Specifically:
- Target net rate: $0.00028/token for tokens within the committed band (9B - 12B monthly)
- Overage rate: $0.00035/token
- Commitment to a 12 month payment term (monthly invoicing)

If you have a standard template for commit tiers or a quick worksheet showing discounts at different volume tiers, please share. Procurement will also ask for a short LOI so they can start internal approvals.

Thanks,
Sanjay
VP Partnerships, HyperCloud Analytics
[Attachment: HyperCloud_MATP_Commits.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@hypercloud.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.m@hypercloud.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing bands and commit question

Sanjay — appreciate the clarity. Short answer: we can do commit-based discounts but anything materially below our published per-token bands requires internal approval (rate-card exception).

I will:
- Share a quick commit-band worksheet (attaching our worksheet)
- Kick off an internal approval with finance and legal for the target net rate you mentioned
- Draft a one-page LOI template that you can use with procurement

Can you confirm whether the 9B/month is a hard floor or a forecasted average? That informs the fallback/overage language.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Commit_Worksheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: HyperCloud pricing: request for custom per-token band + 12mo commit

Team — looping you in. HyperCloud (large public cloud analytics vendor) is asking for a deep per-token discount tied to a 12mo commit: target $0.00028/token at ~9B-12B/month. They are a strategic customer for us in analytics vertical and want an LOI to kick procurement.

Key asks:
- Approve rate-card exception to net $0.00028/token inside the committed band; overage at $0.00035/token
- Contract term: 12 months, monthly invoicing (no pre-pay)
- Right to fallback to published rates if usage falls below 80% of committed volume for two consecutive months

Why approve?
- Volume: If accurate, this is >100M tokens/day and predictable revenue with low support footprint
- Competitive risk: They evaluated other inference vendors with similar pricing offers

Questions for you:
Laura — can finance run model on net margin at that net rate including GPU cost, batching gains, and expected prefix cache lift?
Vivek — any legal guardrails we need for LOI + procurement ask?
Sean — approval on commercial exception (I think this is an above-quota ask)

I'll attach the numbers from HyperCloud's worksheet in a follow-up.

—Rachel
[Attachment: HyperCloud_MATP_Commits.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HyperCloud pricing: request for custom per-token band + 12mo commit

Rachel/Sean — ran a quick P&L on the ask. High level:
- At $0.00028/token net across 9B/month, gross margin compresses but remains positive assuming 1) efficient quantized model variant and 2) sustained batching with 20-30% caching lift.
- If we require monthly invoicing (no up-front), cash flow and bad-debt exposure modestly increase; recommend standard 30-day payment terms and a 60-day credit check with procurement.
- Suggest we structure approval as a tiered discount: first 9B at $0.00030, 9B-12B at $0.00028, >12B at $0.00027 — this reduces downside and preserves upside economics.

If leadership signs off on that banding I can generate an internal rate-card exception approval memo and expected ARR math.

Laura
VP Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@hypercloud.ai>, Elena Morales <elena.m@hypercloud.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing bands and commit question

Hi Sanjay / Elena — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally.

Short summary of what we can provisionally offer (pending final approval):
- 12 month commitment; monthly invoicing; standard 30-day payment terms + procurement credit check
- Pricing (tiered inside the committed volume):
  * 0 - 9B/month: published rate-card applies
  * 9B - 12B/month: $0.00030/token (provisional)
  * >12B/month: $0.00027/token
- Overage if you fall below 80% of committed volume for two consecutive months: published rate-card + 10% premium for that month

If this looks directionally acceptable we can send a one-page LOI and an internal approval packet for your procurement. Can you confirm whether procurement needs any specific contractual language around data residency or audit rights?

Best,
Rachel
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
--

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@hypercloud.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena.m@hypercloud.ai>
Cc: HyperCloud Procurement <procurement@hypercloud.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing bands and commit question

Rachel — thanks for the fast turnaround. That tiered approach is reasonable and gives procurement something they can sign off on. A couple of follow-ups from our side before we start an LOI:
- Procurement asks whether we can get a 45-day payment term instead of 30 days (their standard) — any flexibility?
- They also want a clause that allows a single annual usage reconciliation (true-up) instead of monthly fallbacks; can you flag that with legal?

I'll attach a short LOI and the procurement checklist they use.

Sanjay
VP Partnerships, HyperCloud Analytics
[Attachment: HyperCloud_LOI.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HyperCloud pricing: request for custom per-token band + 12mo commit

Rachel/Team — reviewed the procurement asks. Legal can accept 45-day payment term with two caveats: 1) credit approval required and 2) we add a clause that allows us to suspend service after 75 days overdue.

On the fallback cadence, legal prefers monthly reconciliation for operational simplicity, but we can accommodate an annual reconciliation only if we add a clause for a quarterly usage reporting obligation and an annual true-up with interest on unpaid amounts. I have drafted the LOI addendum language and will drop into the DocuSign template once Sean signs off on the commercial exception.

I am okay to move forward with the tiered banding Laura proposed (9B-12B at $0.00028 was acceptable as a conditional middle band). Please confirm final approval and I will push the LOI through DocuSign.

Vivek
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: LOI_Addendum_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]
